c_lin <= c_part for finite deterministic systems: W_inf subseteq V_Pi*, so dim W_inf <= |Pi*|. Analytical proof; independently enumerated at n=4 (3840 pairs) and n=5 (162500 pairs), 0 violations, gap observed in {0,1} at n=4,5; gap 2 exists at n=6 (see CG-GAP2-COUNTEREXAMPLE); no universal upper bound established.

Two 4-state witnesses, two-block initial partitions, identical c_lin=1 but c_part=1 vs 2 (gap 0 vs 1). Independently replayed. 72 positive-gap cases among 3840 full-partition pairs at n=4; 8160 among 162500 at n=5; 4 states minimal for positive gap; gap is not bounded by 1 in general.

gap = m - rank_Q(M), where m = distinct future block-itineraries and M = itinerary-label matrix. Proven via Cayley-Hamilton reduction and W_inf evaluation on stable classes. Verified: 3840 + 162500 census pairs, 100000-pair stratified n=6 sample, 137400 lifted systems; 0 discrepancies.

Gap 2 exists: n=6 six-cycle T=(1,2,3,4,5,0), partition {{0,1,2},{3,4,5}}. m=6, rank=4, gap=2. Refutes gap<=1 conjecture; mechanism: label word 111000 has cyclic polynomial 1+z+z^2, divisible by z^2+z+1, so circulant rank is 4.

Cyclic 2-block: gap = #missing Fourier modes - (n - m) = m - n + deg gcd(w(z), z^n-1). Independently proved by two models (gcd form and circulant-eigenvalue form); verified 1002 words n=3..9, 0 violations.

Cyclic 2-block systems: the word 1^k 0^k at n=2k has gap k-1=n/2-1, so the closure gap is unbounded with at least linear growth in this family. Exact replay: k=2..8. A tight general growth rate and general upper bound remain open.

Cyclic 2-block max-gap census, exact replay: n=3..11 = [0,1,0,2,0,3,2,4,0]; numpy-rank evaluator (agrees with exact on 6,984 cases) extends to n=14 = [0,1,0,2,0,3,2,4,0,5,0,6]. Even n: max = n/2-1 (n=4..14), achieved by half-half words (exact, k=2..8). Odd n gives 0 for n=3,5,7,11,13 but NOT n=9: max gap 2, e.g. word 000000111.

General (non-cyclic) systems exceed the cyclic max at the same n. Exact examples: gap 1 at n=5 (T=[0,0,0,1,1], partition 01001; exhaustive general max at n=5 is 1 vs cyclic 0), gap 3 at n=7 (T=[1,5,5,1,2,6,6], partition 0011001), gap 4 at n=8 (T=[5,6,6,5,0,2,0,2], partition 00110011). The earlier 'gap-4 at n=7' is NOT replicated: for T=[1,5,5,1,2,6,6] the max over all 877 partitions is 3 (also under 1-based indexing); random+hill-climb search (k=2) found max 3 at n=7. Absence of gap 4 at n=7 is not proved. Tight general upper bound OPEN.

evidence: Proved for all finite deterministic systems: deterministic quotient implies gap=0. Exact exhaustive n=4 (3,840 pairs) and n=5 (162,500 pairs); n=5,6 200k-pair exact sample; zero counterexamples.
note: Positive closure gap requires a non-deterministic quotient. If every block maps into one block, the partition is stable, the coarsest stable refinement has k blocks, and W_inf is the k-dimensional block-constant space, so gap=k-k=0. Hence gap>0 implies at least one block has image-label set of size at least 2. ND is necessary but not sufficient. Balanced-relation formulation: positive gap is equivalent to a nonzero rational left-kernel vector of the itinerary-label matrix; integer bases always exist.

evidence: Exact rational census, n=4 exhaustive (3,840 pairs) and n=5 exhaustive (162,500 pairs), independently replayed in-repo: n=5 positive-gap pairs = 8,160, of which 480 have ND degree exactly 1 and 7,680 have ND degree >=2. Minimal ND-degree-1 witness T=(0,0,1,2,2), lab=(0,1,0,0,1): m=5, rank=4, gap=1, verified exactly.
note: ND>=2 (at least two split blocks) is not sufficient for positive closure gap: at n=5 it misses 480 positive-gap pairs with ND degree exactly 1, and admits 120 gap-0 false positives at n=4 and 22,320 at n=5. No tested graph or partition invariant separates positive-gap from gap-0 with zero false positives at n=4,5; the exact separator remains gap = m - rank_Q(M). This is a finite computational census result, not a general theorem; no novelty claim.
